passage:
In the corridor Mehak grinned at the poster of the leader Jagdish supported and said, "Your hero is a joke." His face burned and he almost shot back an insult. Instead he breathed and asked, "What do you mean by that?" Mehak shrugged and said her father's shop had shut after a new rule. It was not what Jagdish wanted to hear, but it was a reason.

That weekend at dinner his uncle Sohan jabbed a fork at him. "Your lot only repeat slogans." Jagdish's voice climbed to match, until he heard the worry underneath, about Sohan's pension. He said, more quietly, "Can I show you what I read?" When Sohan grew loud again, Jagdish said, "Let's finish this another day, uncle," and left the table politely.

Later, scrolling, he caught himself thinking that everyone on the other side was stupid. It felt good, and there was nobody to tell. On Monday Vidya, who backed the rival party, lent him a pencil, and he asked her why she believed what she did. Her answer was about her mother's clinic, ordinary and thoughtful.

When strangers online called him names over his view and his faith, he did not reply. He blocked them, saved screenshots and showed his teacher. That same day the teacher reported it to the school office.

qa.q: Whose father's shop had shut after a new rule?
qa.a: Mehak's father's shop had shut after a new rule.

qa.q: How did Jagdish's handling of Mehak's mockery differ from his handling of the strangers online?
qa.a: With Mehak he paused and asked what she meant, which let him hear a reason. With the strangers, who were only cruel, he did not reply, but blocked them, saved proof and told his teacher.

qa.q: What was Jagdish feeling when he was sure everyone on the other side was stupid?
qa.a: It felt good to him, but it also left him lonely, since he had nobody to tell.

qa.q: What could Jagdish do next time his uncle gets loud at dinner?
qa.a: He could listen for the worry underneath, keep his facts calm, and leave politely if it gets heated, since the relationship matters more than winning.

grounding: One teen meets political disagreement through anger, a family clash, growing contempt and online abuse, and each is handled differently.
